course_description:
Supervised placement course to develop professional skills in applied psychology. Theories and techniques are applied to build core competencies as a psychologist and in the chosen specialist area of practice endorsement.

The placement component of the postgraduate program is designed to develop skills in workingﾠacross a range of professional competency areas.ﾠStudents undertake placements to gain knowledge, skills, and experience in an applied setting.

This is the fourth placement unit out of four. You are assumed to have completed PSYC7810, PSYC7820, and PSYC7830 beforehand.

prerequisites: You'll need to complete the following courses before enrolling in this one:
Provisional or full registration as a Psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia.
restrictions: Restricted to MPsych or with the permission of Director of the MPsych program

course_aims: Students undertake placements to gain knowledge, skills, and experience in an applied setting. The placement experience forms one part of an integrated program to assist student progress towards full registration as a psychologist in Australia. Due to the nature of the placements, it may be possible not all learning objectives below are covered in this course. All learning objectivesﾠwill be met throughout all four of placement courses.

learning_outcomes.description: Applies and builds scientific knowledge of psychology to inform safe and effective practice Demonstrates foundational knowledge of psychological theories, research methods, and evidence-based practice. Critically evaluates scientific literature, research principles, and culturally informed practice to guide clinical decision-making and professional practice.

Practises ethically and professionally Takes responsibility for professional conduct aligned with ethical standards and legal requirements. Practises within boundaries of competence, manages risks appropriately, and seeks consultation when needed. Demonstrates digital competence.

Exercises professional reflexivity, purposeful and deliberate practice, and self-care Engages in critical self-reflection regarding one’s own culture, values, biases, and their impact on practice. Actively identifies areas for professional development and maintains self-care to sustain effective functioning.

Conducts psychological assessments Selects, administers, and interprets culturally appropriate assessment methods across the lifespan. Collaboratively develops goals with clients, formulates results, and provides meaningful feedback based on results.

Conducts psychological interventions Implements evidence-based, culturally safe interventions appropriate to client needs and context. Outlines risks and benefits to clients. Regularly evaluates intervention effectiveness and adjusts approaches based on client progress and feedback.

Communicates and relates to others effectively and appropriately Establishes and maintains professional, safe, respectful relationships with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders. Communicates clearly using appropriate modes of delivery (includes digital) and works collaboratively with other professionals.

Demonstrates a health equity and human rights approach when working with people from diverse groups Works inclusively and respectfully with people from diverse backgrounds, recognising intersecting forms of diversity. Understands and applies cultural responsiveness, trauma-informed care, and adapts practice to meet diverse client needs.

Demonstrates a health equity and human rights approach when working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, families and communities Understands the historical and ongoing impacts of colonisation and applies culturally safe, trauma-informed practice. Works in partnership with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, respecting self-determination and consulting appropriately.

assessment_details.due_date: 23/03/2026 5:00 pm Placement Contract is due 2 weeks after the initial Principal Supervisor meeting following placement confirmation. If this date is after the date outlined above, the Contract is due by the date outlined in the Course Profile ("date above").
assessment_details.task_description: Placement confirmation generally occurs when the organisation agrees to take the provisional psychologist/student on placement; this may be at placement allocation or after an initial interview/meeting. Following confirmation, the provisional psychologist/student is required to organise an initial meeting with the Principal Supervisor to complete the Placement Contract, formalising the agreed arrangements. Your first meeting with your supervisor is to discuss and record (using the Contract) the specific responsibilities of both you and your supervisor during the placement, placement schedule/timeline, specific goals or competencies you wish to focus on, projects you or the organisation may have in mind, and any other considerations. Please state these points clearly in the Placement Contract Placement Contract must include the signature of your Principal Supervisor as well as Secondary and Tertiary supervisors if required (e.g., on-site line manager if Principal Supervisor is Longarm). The Placement Manager will sign the Contract with signature via Blackboard submission. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.task_description: Placement folios will differ in content for each student, depending on students’ unique placement experiences. Only one main folio item and one organisational project description needs to be included in the folio. A Folio Checklist included in templates is provided and is submitted as a table of contents in your folio. The order of the Folio is as follows: Completed and Signed Folio Cover Sheet Completed Title Page Completed Placement Folio Checklist (Table of Contents) Summary of Placement Hours Form Section 1: Placement description and reflection Section 2: Main folio item Section 3: Organisational project report Section 4: Logs and other placement forms Section 5: Placement Contract and Signed Reviews Refer to the Master of Psychology Placement Handbook for full details. assessment_details.title: Professional Development Log
assessment_details.due_date: Logs must be reviewed regularly by supervisor(s) and submitted in the folio at the end of each placement (4 weeks after the end of placement activities).
assessment_details.task_description: Provisional Psychologists must maintain logs that details activities undertaken during the placement. The logbook provides a mechanism for recording and reporting on the three key components of the placement: direct client activities, client related (other) activities, and supervision. The logs also serve as a means to monitor progress and adherence to the Placement Contract, so that any challenges can be identified and addressed early on. Logs must be reviewed regularly by supervisor(s) and submitted in the folio at the end of each placement. Failure to maintain a completed logbook may result in failure of placement. Every entry in the supervision log must have a corresponding Record of Supervision form. Records of Supervision provide details regarding the content discussed during supervision sessions, including any action items or areas for improvement. All Records of Supervision must be signed by provisional psychologist and supervisor. Refer to the Master of Psychology Placement Handbook for in depth information about logs. learning_activities.topic: Group and Peer Supervision (GAPS) Group and Peer Supervision (GAPS) is a two-year program designed to provide additional support translating coursework into practice while students are on placement. The aim is for GAPS to allow provisional psychologists to come together, share, learn, grow, practice, support and challenge each other. Therefore, the sessions will be working towards more interactive, integrative, and reflective than is possible in other course activities. The aim is to develop a space for activities that may include case presentations by provisional psychologists. GAPS schedule will be provided at the start of Semester. Learning outcomes: L01, L04, L06, L07, L08, L09, L10
